lines.text: Jesus comes down and stands on a level place, and the crowd is HUGE: people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon. They came to hear Him and to be healed, and everybody's trying to touch Him, because power is coming from Him and healing them all.

Jesus looks up at His disciples: blessed are you who are poor, you who hunger now, you who weep now. Then He flips the whole tray over: woe to you who are rich, you who are well fed now, you who laugh now, and woe when all men speak well of you.

Now the TOUGH part: love your enemies, turn the other cheek, give to everyone who asks, and lend expecting nothing in return. Do that, and your reward will be great, and you'll be sons of Abraham. So be merciful, just as your Father is merciful. Friend, I'm still working on the cheek one.

Don't judge, don't condemn, forgive. Give, and a good measure, pressed down and running over, gets poured into your lap. And before you go after the speck in your brother's eye, get the BEAM out of your own. Each tree is known by its own fruit, and out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.

Why call Him Lord, Lord and not do what He says? The one who hears and acts is like a man who dug down deep and built on the rock, and the flood couldn't shake it. The one who hears and doesn't act built his house on the sand, and when the torrent hit, it fell immediately. Great was its destruction.

wrong_details.wrong: built his house on the sand
wrong_details.true: built his house on ground without a foundation
